criteria.criterion: met - no maxlength attribute, maxLength -1 on create and edit textareas; insertText of 237 and 250 chars kept value.length 237 and 250.
met - initial 0/200; 100/200 after insertText; edit opened on 250-char post reads 250/200 at once.
met - 150 emoji (length 300) reads 150/200; 200 emoji valid; 201 emoji blocked; 200 chars padded with spaces (raw 205) reads 200/200, no error.
met - at 200: no over-limit class, no aria-invalid, message hidden, Save enabled. At 201 all effects appear.

met - 237: "Description is too long: 237/200 characters. Remove 37 characters to post."; 201 uses "Remove 1 character"; aria-invalid=true; aria-describedby includes message id; static aria-live=polite wrapper in DOM before message; counter color rgb(179,18,42) vs normal rgb(83,100,113).
met - Save disabled=true, no aria-busy, label "Save" (create and edit).

met - over limit: requestSubmit(), Enter key in textarea, and dispatched submit event produced zero POST/PUT in Network log; #form-error stayed hidden. Edit form requestSubmit over limit: zero requests.
met - back to 200 in the same input: message empty/hidden, aria-invalid absent, Save enabled; edit trimmed from 250 to 200 enables Save.
met - after real successful create on temp server: 0/200, no error, no aria-invalid, Save enabled, list shows 2 posts.

met - edit on seeded 250-char post (inserted in temp DB): immediately 250/200 error, message "Remove 50 characters", aria-invalid, Save disabled; normal post shows 15/200 with no error. Cancel removes form; reopen is fresh.
met - create Save stayed enabled and unmarked while edit was over; only one .edit-form after opening a second edit.
met - textarea still required; whitespace-only reads 0/200, no error.

met - Fetch-fulfilled 422 on POST shows "Couldn't save your log: description must be at most 200 characters. Shorten your description to 200 characters or fewer and try again."; Save re-enabled, label Save.
met - measured from computed colors vs body bg. Light: normal 6.12, over 6.92, message 6.92. Dark: normal 7.13, over 9.50, message 9.50. Edit form counter/message same values in both themes.

met - at 360px: no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth == clientWidth, 360 or 345 when vertical scrollbar shown); counter, message, textarea, Save rects do not intersect and are within 0..360 in create normal/over and edit normal/over; edit counter gap below textarea is +6px (negative margin does not overlap). Screenshots reviewed.

met - Tab order textarea, file input, Save, then next button with solid 3px focus-visible outline; aria-busy "Saving..." with disabled during held POST, and typing over-limit text during the save did not clear busy.
met - backend pytest 130 passed; project file hashes (excluding .venv and .claude) identical before and after my runs; only frontend files have recent mtime; no new files or caches created.

met - port 8765 verified free via netstat; GET /api/logs returned [] before any write; used create_app(temp_db, temp_uploads) from a script in scratchpad; real logs.db sha256 and uploads unchanged; Chrome killed only by temp profile path, server stopped, ports released.

verification.runtime_check: Real app served from create_app on temp port 8765 with temp DB/uploads, driven by headless Chrome via CDP: typing/paste with Input.insertText, Network event recording, Fetch interception (422 and held POST), prefers-color-scheme emulation, 360px device metrics, real create/edit/delete/cancel flows. Screenshots in scratchpad t010-shots (6 files) viewed: counter and message legible, ring visible, Save dimmed with explanatory message, 360px layout intact.
verification.self_critique: One check failed in my script: it expected the over-limit text typed during an in-flight save to survive; the save succeeded and form.reset() cleared it (0/200, Save enabled, label Save, no busy), which is correct existing behavior, so I treated it as a test-expectation error. Not tested: real screen-reader announcements (only aria-live structure), focus ring appearance of hover rules under real fine pointer, non-Chrome browsers, exotic whitespace differences between JS trim and Python strip, forced-colors mode. Edit tests used photo-less seeded post plus a post with a 1x1 PNG.
